html:
TikTok Shop affiliate commission is the percentage a brand pays a creator on each sale the creator drives, set by the brand in the Affiliate Center, earned when a customer buys through the creator's content, and typically landing between 10% and 20%. It is how creators get paid without holding inventory and how brands turn creators into a sales force. Here is the mechanic, plainly.

Who sets it and who pays it

The brand sets the commission rate on a product or category inside the Affiliate Center. The brand pays it out of the sale price when a creator drives a purchase. TikTok handles the attribution and payout tracking, so neither side manages it manually.

The upside is what motivates creators to keep posting on commission alone. Claims of outlier earnings circulate constantly, like one marketer's "$75,000 in commission from one" viral video (@ashercrw on X). Those are outliers, not the norm, but they explain why creators will run pure-commission deals: a single hit can dwarf a month of flat fees.

When it is earned

A creator earns commission when a customer buys the product through the creator's shoppable content or link, within TikTok's attribution window. If the sale is refunded or cancelled, the commission does not stand. This is one reason GMV is not revenue: commission and refunds both sit between the headline number and what the brand keeps.

Open vs Target commission

  • Open Collaboration: the brand sets a public rate any eligible creator can take. Same rate for all.
  • Target Collaboration: the brand can offer a specific creator a custom rate, often alongside free product. See Open vs Target.

Standard rates

Most categories run 10% to 20%, depending on margin and how much recruiting muscle the brand needs. Newer brands often pay higher to attract creators; established products with proof pay less. Full detail on where the numbers land by category in commission rates by category, and how to set your own in setting commission rates.

What brands should understand

  • Commission is your main recruiting lever; set it deliberately by margin.
  • It comes out of your contribution, so know your true per-unit numbers first.
  • A strong commission plus a converting product is the offer; neither works alone.

What creators should understand

  • You earn only on attributed, completed sales.
  • Higher-commission products are not always more profitable to promote; conversion and price matter as much as the rate.
  • Consistent posting compounds earnings more than chasing the single highest rate.

The takeaway

Affiliate commission is a brand-set percentage paid on creator-driven sales, usually 10% to 20%, earned on completed purchases and handled automatically by TikTok. Understand it as the lever that aligns brand and creator incentives, and set or evaluate it with the real economics in view.

Want commission strategy handled as part of a full program? Book a call, or find creators to recruit.
